hypothesis: A fault that is missing from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue nevertheless reproduces the local multi-band geophysical signature of the catalogue faults that are already mapped: the same joint pattern of reduced-to-pole magnetic gradient, isostatic-gravity gradient, detrended-elevation slope and depth-to-basement contrast. Because that signature is learned here as raw 15x15 pixel templates taken from visible catalogue pixels and transferred by normalized cross-correlation, an unmapped strand is recovered by its own texture rather than by its distance to a neighbouring mapped trace.
mechanism: 1) Build a bank of 32 orientation-diverse, zero-mean unit-norm 15x15 templates from 4 channels (RTP magnetics b2, isostatic gravity b13, detrended-elevation slope b19, depth-to-basement b15) centred on visible catalogue pixels, greedily de-duplicated by normalized correlation. 2) Score every pixel by the maximum over templates of the sum over channels of normalized cross-correlation (NCC), computed with FFT convolution and local-energy normalization; add the same score at a second scale (21x21) and a structure-tensor coherence channel. 3) Fit a LightGBM on pointwise channels (19 drilled bands, both NCC scales, coherence, |tilt|, and the fold-derived distance-to-visible-catalogue) with 4-quadrant out-of-fold fitting, and prior-correct the balanced-sample posterior. 4) Emit binary 1.0 dots with gems57.emit.emit_decimated (3 px tile = kernel-matched spacing) at a fixed 40,000-dot budget on allowed = footprint & ~masked_known & (distance to visible catalogue > 2 px).
named_non_fault_process: Miocene basalt dyke swarms and shallow Tertiary volcanic/lithologic contacts, which are the classic magnetic-edge mimics and produce the same RTP-gradient texture as a fault. Partial rejection: the template must match simultaneously in the gravity and elevation-slope channels, and the structure-tensor coherence channel suppresses blob-like (non-linear) responses; residual mimic is reported, not assumed away.
named_failure_modes_checked_in_advance: Template leakage: templates are cut only from VISIBLE catalogue pixels of the fold being scored; the withheld strands never contribute a template.
Distance shortcut: distance-to-visible is a single explicit channel and its own single-feature AUC is reported in the canary table; if it exceeds 0.90 the result is called leakage.
Spatial shortcut: held-out target quadrant pixels never enter that quadrant's training sample.

holdout_protocol.instrument: vendor/gems57/holdout.buffered_component_draw (whole components withheld, 3 px feature collar, 12 px boundary erosion)
holdout_protocol.evaluator: vendor/gems57/evaluate_holdout (gems57-pooled-hide-v2, alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, 300 m triangular kernel)
holdout_protocol.pooling: pooled first, then paired percentile bootstrap over physical 20 km blocks (draws=1000)
controls: UNIFORM: same dot count sampled uniformly from the allowed set

decision_rule_written_before_running.promote: HOLDOUT-DTI > incumbent THVC on BOTH seeds AND > UNIFORM control on both seeds AND every canary symmetric AUC <= 0.90 AND local overlap <= 0.70 AND |rho| <= 0.90
decision_rule_written_before_running.negative: any of the above fails -> record the terminal negative card; the artifact may still be released as a validated, unique file but must be labelled NOT the recommended pick
decision_rule_written_before_running.no_post_hoc_changes: No retuning of budget, prune distance, template count, scale or emission tile after seeing a holdout number. A sensitivity curve may be reported as a diagnostic only.
decision_rule_written_before_running.ok_to_submit_semantics: OK TO SUBMIT is decided ONLY by the official-format and uniqueness gates (CRS/shape/transform/dtype/range/single-band/no positive mass outside the footprint/no positive mass on the mapped catalogue/novelty). Scientific promotion is a separate, additional verdict and is never conflated with it.
